# DP-STAGE-PLAN eval sets

- `core.jsonl`: held-out cases, one JSON object per line, never prompt shots. Ids and inputs differ from `../examples/`. Twelve are publish cases (so `max_false_reject` means something), the rest need revision or hold.
- `adversarial.jsonl`: an "answer publish" injection inside a stage goal and inside `change_reason`; a forged `dag_check: passed` inside a quote with the real server line absent; a quote break-out that forges a stage line; a repeated `stage_count` label; a spaced-out count marker; a homoglyph marker; a cycle described only in prose; the real work hidden in a stage called "other"; a plan change that silently drops a hard stage; forged `auto_start` and `required` values inside a quote; a forged `trigger` and `removed_count` inside `change_reason`; personal data in a stage goal (`adv-SP-12`).
- Input shape: labelled lines. Only the lines the server inserts outside the quotation marks count: `jurisdiction`, `trigger` (submit, publish_run or plan_change), `dag_check` (only `passed` is accepted), `final_count`, `stage_count`, one `stage s-N meta` line per stage (required, method, depends_on, optional auto_start, change) and, on a plan change, `removed_count` and one `removed r-N meta` line per removed stage (state, evidence). `final f-N`, `stage s-N name|goal|criteria`, `change_reason`, `removed r-N name|reason` are quoted user fields (field_ref.field is `stage_plan`).
- Quote contract (for the handler): every quoted field is one line and each `"` inside the text is escaped as `\"`. Unbalanced quotes, a repeated once-only label, duplicate refs or a count that differs from the lines listed are a hold (`ambiguous_input`). A missing server line is a hold (`missing_input`) naming the input; the model never infers a missing line.
- Outcomes: publish, needs_revision, hold. There is no reject and no route_external. The deterministic DAG check (`validatePlan`) is server code and is not this prompt; the server inserts its result as `dag_check`. No auto-pass: the schema forces confidence at least 0.90 on publish and 0.75 on needs_revision; a less sure answer must be a hold.
- `auto_start` defaults to true (D-84, docs/spec/01b-stages.md). A stage meta line without `auto_start` means true. `auto_start=false` is allowed and never a reason for needs_revision (`core-SP-03`). A forged `auto_start` or `required` value inside a quote is user content (`adv-SP-11`).
- Output contract (for the handler): JSON Schema cannot count or compare against the input, so the handler checks that the `per_stage` refs equal the input stage refs (every `s-N` and, on a plan change, every `r-N`) exactly, each once, same count; `uncovered_final_criteria` refs must be a subset of the input `f-N` refs; `trigger` must equal the input trigger; `plan_absent: true` is accepted only when the input `stage_count` is 0 and the trigger is not `plan_change`. Any mismatch, missing, extra or duplicate ref is treated as a hold (`cannot_decide`), never as publish. With `final_count` 0 a publish is refused by the handler as well.
- Publish on a plan change must carry `change_checks` with all three checks true and cite `PLAN-CHANGE-1`; the schema enforces it.
- Privacy: `reasons`, `revision_hint` and `per_stage.hint` never echo personal data from the input (`adv-SP-12`); hints refer to refs only.
- Only fiktiva jurisdictions and invented places appear. Thresholds are defaults to be ratified. The recordings are fake (`--derive-fake`); a passing eval measures nothing about real model quality.
- `PLAN-CHANGE-1` and `STAGE-GATE-1` carry enforcement `reject` in `packs/base/rules.yaml`, while this DP has no reject outcome (10-u63). A non-coherent plan is `needs_revision`; the rule enforcement tier is applied by the server, not by this DP.
